data.title: Powering Ahead: Sungrow Demonstrates Resilience and Innovation at RE+ 2026
data.description:
Powering Ahead: Sungrow Demonstrates Resilience and Innovation at RE+ 2026

Powering Ahead: Sungrow Demonstrates Resilience and Innovation at RE+ 2026

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sungrow, a globally leading PV inverter and energy storage system provider, showcased its latest energy technologies and solutions at RE+ 2026, addressing the evolving energy needs of the North American market. Highlights included the latest advancements in Safety of Utility-scale Energy Storage, Integrated Power Solutions for AI data centers, and an Enhanced Modular Inverter for utility-scale solar, and flexible energy storage solutions for commercial and industrial (C&I) applications.

PowerTitan 3.0: Advancing Large-Scale Energy Storage Safety

A major highlight at RE+ was the first public presentation of Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 Large-Scale Fire Test (LSFT) video, offering attendees an inside look at its system-level safety validation.

In October 2026, PowerTitan 3.0 successfully completed a large-scale fire test. The test was conducted under the lead of UL Solutions, with Fire Risk Alliance (FRA) and Jensen Hughes (JH) present. It marks the industry's first large-scale fire test of a stacked-cell BESS featuring an integrated AC-block design, demonstrating Sungrow's continued commitment to advancing energy storage safety.

Beyond safety, PowerTitan 3.0 delivers high efficiency and rapid deployment for utility-scale energy storage applications. The system achieves up to 99.3% power conversion efficiency and 92% round-trip efficiency (RTE), helping minimize energy losses throughout the charge and discharge cycles.

Its stacked battery cell design helps reduce the risks of overheating and short circuits. Combined with self-monitoring capabilities, the system manages potential thermal risks with over 99% warning accuracy, supporting safer and more reliable operation.

Designed for rapid deployment, PowerTitan 3.0 features factory pre-assembly and pre-testing to reduce on-site installation and commissioning effort. A 1 GWh project can be grid-connected in as short as 12 days, helping accelerate project delivery and improve overall deployment efficiency.

Integrated Power Solutions for AI Data Centers

As AI data centers drive growing demand for reliable and high-efficiency power infrastructure, Sungrow presented its integrated power solutions featuring the EnerNeo Solid-State Transformer (SST) and a range of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) based power supply architectures for AI Data Centers application.

Sungrow offers EnerNeo Solid State Transformer (SST), designed to make power delivery simpler and more efficient. The modular design EnerNeo SST offers 1.5–6 MW power range and simplifies power delivery by converting medium-voltage AC directly into 800V DC. Complementing the SST, Sungrow presented three BESS architectures tailored to different data center power requirements: Grid-Forming (GFM) BESS, MV-UPS + BESS, and Dual-PCS + BESS. Built on different approaches to power management, these solutions support dynamic load smoothing, grid support, and power resilience. Together, they offer data center operators flexible options to address increasingly complex power challenges as AI infrastructure scales.

Optimized 4.8 MW Modular Inverter for Utility-Scale Solar

Sungrow also showcased its optimized 4.8 MW SG4800UD-MV-US modular inverter for the North American utility-scale solar market. Combining the advantages of central and string inverter technologies, the solution delivers 1.6 MW per unit in a flexible modular design, helping reduce balance-of-system (BOS) costs.

The split modular design enables inverter module replacement in under an hour, minimizing downtime and improving operational efficiency. Smart DC terminal temperature protection and a bottom pressure relief design further strengthen system safety. The inverter also features PV grid-forming and off-grid commissioning capabilities, supporting earlier commercial operation and helping improve project returns.

PowerStack 255CS: Supporting North America's Growing C&I Market

As Sungrow continues to expand its presence in the North American C&I energy storage market, the company showcased the PowerStack 255CS integrated energy storage system with built-in PCS.

The system delivers 257 kWh of capacity in a two-hour configuration. Designed for versatile applications, the PowerStack 255CS supports standalone energy storage, PV-plus-storage systems, EV charging integration, and microgrids. It also accommodates off-grid applications, providing a flexible energy solution for businesses seeking to enhance power reliability and maintain critical operations.

Powering North America's Energy Future

From AI data centers, utility-scale energy storage to solar power generation and C&I applications, Sungrow continues to develop technologies that address the increasingly diverse needs of the North American energy landscape.

Through its ongoing innovation in power conversion, energy storage, and grid-forming technologies, Sungrow remains committed to supporting North America's evolving energy infrastructure with efficient, reliable, and adaptable solutions.

About Sungrow

Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has pioneered sustainable power solutions for over 29 years. As of June 2026, Sungrow has installed 1100 GW of power electronic converters worldwide. The Company is recognized as the world's most bankable PV inverter and energy storage company (BloombergNEF). Its innovations power clean energy projects across the globe, supported by a network of 520 service outlets guaranteeing excellent customer experience. At Sungrow, we're committed to bridging to a sustainable future through cutting-edge technology and unparalleled service. For more information, please visit: www.sungrowpower.com/en

data.title: Asian Equities Decline as Caution Prevails
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities were broadly lower Thursday morning as firmed expectations of higher interest rates inspired little demand for stocks and sentiment stayed cautious.

Investors are digesting hawkish-sounding minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, and looking ahead to the trilateral summit between U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Trump and Xi are also scheduled for a separate bilateral meeting. The meetings represent the highest-level diplomatic engagement in months and will be closely watched for any signals on trade, technology restrictions, and the broader geopolitical framework affecting Asian markets," Commerzbank Research analysts said.

Anthropic's trading debut is also in focus, seen as a major test of appetite for artificial-intelligence trades after the Nvidia scandal sparked another wave of selloffs in the technology sector.

Concerns about the impact of tightened U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continue to weigh on tech and AI-related stocks in Asia.

Fragile risk sentiment was evident across major indexes.

South Korea's Kospi gave up early gains to turn lower during the morning session, and was recently down 0.9%. Taiwan's Taiex was off by 2.7%, while Chinese benchmarks were in the red. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average swung between gains and losses and was last 0.1% higher.

In Hong Kong, major tech names posted sharp drops, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index 2.1% lower.

Elsewhere, crude oil futures were mixed after Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday, while continuing attacks against ships seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate futures edged 0.1% lower to $83.15 a barrel and front-month Brent rose 0.3% to $92.21 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Gold recovered some ground, rising 0.7%, but stayed around its lowest levels in over on year at $3,750.18 an ounce. Silver also bounced back but stayed weak.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

November 18, 2026 21:46 ET (02:46 GMT)

data.title: Hot Dog Marketing Sharpens Focus on Public Sector, Taps Central Texas Leaders to Guide Growth
data.description:
Hot Dog Marketing Sharpens Focus on Public Sector, Taps Central Texas Leaders to Guide Growth

Hot Dog Marketing Sharpens Focus on Public Sector, Taps Central Texas Leaders to Guide Growth

PR Newswire

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 18, 2026

Agency expands strategic communications capabilities and establishes five-member Strategic Advisory Council to strengthen its position in public-sector markets.

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hot Dog Marketing, a Central Texas-based marketing and communications agency, is sharpening its focus on professional services firms, government contractors and public entities. The firm announced a new strategic communications offering and the formation of a five-member Strategic Advisory Council composed of established Central Texas business and civic leaders.

The move marks a new chapter for the agency as it builds on its established foundation to help clients become better known and trusted in the markets they serve.

"Organizations working in and around the public sector face unique challenges when it comes to building visibility, establishing credibility and communicating their value," said Jessica Scanlon, founder and CEO of Hot Dog Marketing. "We're expanding our capabilities to help clients address those challenges more strategically while continuing to provide the marketing expertise that has been central to our business."

Through the new offerings, the company aims to provide clients with an integrated approach that will help them communicate their value more effectively and build stronger reputations. The focus is on developing relationships with public-sector decision-makers and strengthening firms' presence in their target industries.

The Strategic Advisory Council brings together five leaders whose backgrounds span public infrastructure and professional services, with deep ties to the Central Texas business community.

The council includes:

  • Lynda Rife, founder of Rifeline, with more than 35 years of experience in public involvement, government relations and community engagement.
  • Mike Heiligenstein, former executive director of the Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority, with decades of experience in public infrastructure, government leadership and regional planning.
  • Ali Khataw, founder and CEO of Encotech Engineering Consultants and longtime Central Texas business and civic leader with extensive experience in engineering, entrepreneurship and community development.
  • Jordan Robinson, president and CEO of the Round Rock Chamber, with expertise in economic development, business attraction and regional partnerships.
  • Bryant Smith, managing director of McCreary Veselka Bragg & Allen (MVBA), with extensive experience in organizational leadership, operations and strategic business growth.

Advisory council members will provide strategic guidance to Hot Dog Marketing's leadership as the agency responds to evolving client needs and explores new opportunities to strengthen its position in the Texas market.

"Each of these leaders brings a perspective that will challenge our thinking and help us grow intentionally," Scanlon said. "Our goal is bigger than growing an agency. We want to build a stronger organization that helps our clients grow, creates meaningful opportunities for our team and makes a positive impact in the communities we serve."

About Hot Dog Marketing

Hot Dog Marketing is a Central Texas-based marketing and strategic communications agency specializing in professional services firms, government contractors, public entities and economic development organizations. The minority- and woman-owned agency combines branding, digital marketing, creative services and strategic communications to help organizations build visibility, strengthen credibility and support business growth.

Learn more at https://hotdogmarketing.com/.

Swell Partners Wins Two 2026 Stevie® Awards for Women in Business

Swell Partners Wins Two 2026 Stevie® Awards for Women in Business

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 18, 2026

Company of the Year, Business Services and Best Female CEO of the Year awards recognize Swell's people-first culture and leadership

NEW YORK, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Swell Partners, a leading provider of talent solutions and business consulting, is proud to announce that it has won two 2026 Stevie® Awards for Women in Business: Company of the Year -Business Services and Best Female CEO of the Year, recognizing founder and CEO Cari Gatto.

The Stevie Awards, which has been hailed as the world's premier business award, honor the achievements of women executives, entrepreneurs, employees, and the companies they lead. These honors celebrate Swell Partners' continued growth and the leadership philosophy behind its success: that exceptional business results and a positive workplace culture go hand in hand. 

"These awards are especially meaningful because they recognize both our company and the people-first values that guide us," said Cari Gatto, Founder and CEO of Swell Partners. "At Swell, we believe that when people feel valued, supported, and connected to meaningful work, they find a greater sense of purpose, bring their best selves to work, and make a lasting impact on the teams and businesses they support. I'm incredibly proud of our team and the relationships we've built with our consultants and clients." 

Swell's vision is to create a world of happy work people and happy workplaces. Its personalized approach combines talent expertise, technology, and meaningful human connection to help hiring leaders and professionals bring out the best in each other.

The Stevie recognition adds to a milestone year for Swell Partners. In 2026, the company was named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies for the fifth consecutive year, ranking No. 294 among New York companies. Swell was also named as one of Inc. magazine's Best Workplaces in 2026.

Entries from organizations and individuals in 56 nations and territories were submitted for consideration. Stevie Award winners are determined by a formal scoring process from more than 200 judges.

Details about the Stevie Awards for Women in Business and the list of winners are available at Women.StevieAwards.com.

About Swell Partners 

Founded in 2013, Swell Partners is a talent solutions and consulting company on a mission to create a world of happy work people and happy workplaces. Swell helps leading organizations build high-performing teams by connecting them with exceptional talent who fit their culture, deliver results, and contribute to a positive, collaborative workplace. Combining talent expertise, technology, and the power of human connection, Swell takes a highly personalized approach to matching people with organizations where both businesses and individuals can thrive. Swell's commitment to creating happiness, fostering purposeful work, and building lasting relationships has contributed to its recognition on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for five consecutive years, its selection as a 2026 Inc. magazine's Best Workplace, and two 2026 Stevie® Awards for Women in Business, including Company of the Year, Business Services and Best Female CEO of the Year.

About the Stevie® Awards

Stevie Awards are conferred in nine programs: the Asia-Pacific Stevie Awards, the German Stevie Awards, the Middle East & North Africa Stevie Awards, The American Business Awards®, The International Business Awards®, the Stevie Awards for Great Employers, the Stevie Awards for Sales & Customer Service, the Stevie Awards for Technology Excellence, and the Stevie Awards for Women in Business. Stevie Awards competitions receive more than 12,000 entries each year from organizations in more than 70 nations and territories. Honoring organizations of all types and sizes and the people behind them, the Stevies recognize outstanding performances in the workplace worldwide. Learn more at www.StevieAwards.com.

data.title: Talisker Provides Ore Sorter Facility Construction Update for the Bralorne Gold Project
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Talisker Resources Ltd. ("Talisker" or the "Company") (TSX: TSK, OTCQX: TSKFF) is pleased to provide an update on the continued advancement of its ore sorter facility (“Sorting Facility”) at the Company’s 100% owned Bralorne Gold Project (“Bralorne”).   Construction and engineering activities have continued to advance according to plan, with several major project milestones already completed and a number of critical work programs now entering the execution phase.

Key Highlights:

  • Initial operation of the Sorting Facility is targeted for Q2 2027, with full commissioning expected in July-August 2027.
  • Electrical infrastructure is completed and targeted for commissioning by the end of November 2026, providing power for the future operation of the Sorting Facility.
  • Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorting Facility were successfully completed in September.
  • Phase 2 earthworks and concrete foundation construction is planned to commence late November 2026, following removal of legacy infrastructure.
  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of the TOMRA XRT Sorter is scheduled for early December 2026, with the ore sorter expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.
  • Major long-lead equipment procurement is substantially complete, with the jaw crusher, cone crusher, vibrating screen plant received in Bralorne in October, conveyors, compressors, and buildings being delivered in phases starting December 2026.
  • Construction and mechanical installation activities are planned throughout Q1 2027, supported by completion of detailed engineering and issuance of the remaining construction tender packages in December 2026.

Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorter Facility was successfully completed in September. The electrical infrastructure has been procured and installed, with final commissioning scheduled for the end of November 2026. The Mustang Mine power generation and distribution system consists of two 1.5 MW diesel generators, providing a total installed generation capacity of 3 MW at 600 V. The generators can operate in parallel or independently, providing redundancy and backup capability.

Power for the underground mining operations is stepped up to 4.16 kV through a 3,200 kVA transformer and distributed to underground substations that will supply mining equipment.

Surface power distribution is installed and ready to serve the sorting and crushing facilities, as well as supporting all other surface infrastructure requirements. The electrical system incorporates protective switchgear, circuit breakers, ground-fault monitoring, and neutral grounding resistors to ensure safe and reliable operation during the next phase of project development. The power plant and distribution network have also been designed to accommodate the future addition of a third generator unit, allowing for straightforward expansion of site power capacity as operational requirements increase.

As part of the ore sorter site preparation activities, a legacy electrical system located within the planned Sorting Facility footprint has been safely dismantled and removed, clearing part of the area for Phase 2 Earthworks construction. In parallel, the Company has completed construction of a new tension-fabric steel frame heavy-duty mechanic shop and is currently transitioning operations from the legacy shop. Demolition of the former shop is expected to be completed in November, fully opening the sorter site for Phase 2 Earthworks before the end of November.

The Phase 2 Earthworks and concrete contractor is scheduled to mobilize to site in November, marking the beginning of a major construction phase. This work will include cut-and-fill activities, foundation preparation, and pre-cast concrete installation within the area previously occupied by the legacy electrical infrastructure and mechanic shop.

Detailed engineering for the project continues to progress well. Issue-for-Tender packages covering the remaining construction components including equipment installation, electrical and mechanical are expected to be completed in December 2026, positioning the project for construction execution through the first half of 2027.

Procurement efforts have been highly successful, with all major equipment purchased. Equipment is either in manufacturing or pending delivery. A proactive approach to early procurement has significantly de-risked the project schedule and supports the Company's objective of maintaining construction momentum throughout the coming months.

A key milestone will occur during the second week of December when the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is conducted for the TOMRA XRT sorter. Following successful testing, the ore sorter is expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.

The crushing circuit has also reached an important milestone, with all major crushing equipment including the jaw crusher, cone crusher, and vibrating screen plant, now delivered and in Bralorne. The compressor system required to support sorter operations is expected to ship for delivery in January 2027.

Building fabrication remains on track, with the manufacturing of two tension-fabric steel frame buildings completed and ready for shipment. The remaining two buildings are expected to be completed and shipped in January 2027.

Engineering and fabrication of the conveyor systems is progressing well. Initial conveyor deliveries are expected to begin arriving on site in mid-December, with additional conveyors being manufactured and shipped in priority sequence throughout the first quarter of 2027.

Taken together, these achievements represent substantial progress toward delivery of one of the Company's most important infrastructure projects. The project continues to transition from planning into full-scale execution with detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities advancing simultaneously.

The Sorting Facility remains on schedule for operational readiness in the second quarter of 2027, with full commissioning anticipated during July-August 2027. Pre-commissioning activities will involve sorting existing stockpile inventory, providing an opportunity to validate system performance ahead of full scale operations. Once operational, the Sorting Facility will process run-of-mine material and is expected to enhance gold grades while eliminating dilution prior to trucking and shipping, improve operating efficiencies, reduce transportation costs, and strengthen project economics.

Terry Harbort, President and CEO, stated, "We are very pleased with the progress being made on the Sorting Facility. With key infrastructure completed, major equipment secured, and construction activities continuing to ramp up, the project remains on schedule for operational readiness in Q2 2027. This Sorting Facility represents an important milestone for Bralorne and will play a significant role in improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's long-term growth objectives."


Figure 1: Aerial view of the Mustang Mine site with a rendered overlay of the sorting facility. The recently completed machine shop and the Mustang Mine power generation systems are shown to scale in their actual locations. The Sorting Facility rendering is provided for conceptual illustration only and may not be to scale. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence from 1 through 4.


Figure 2: 3D rendering of the Sorting Facility. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence. Run-of-mine material is loaded into the jaw crusher (1) via the loading ramp and conveyed to the triple-deck screening plant (2). Screened material is then transported to the TOMRA XRT sorter (3), where gold-bearing material is separated from waste rock. The sorted product is conveyed to the cone crusher (4) before being stockpiled within a covered tension-fabric storage building. Waste reject material is conveyed to a separate waste stockpile.


Figure 3: Mustang Mine and Sorting Facility Power Generation System will power all Mustang Operations including the ore sorter, with 100% redundancy.


Figure 4: Left, the Mustang Mine and Sorter Facility power generation system in the foreground, and the new tension-fabric steel frame mechanic shop in the centre background. Right, the new Mustang Mine Mechanic shop.


Figure 5: The Jaw Crusher, Cone Crusher, vibrating screen plant and all crushing circuit equipment frames arrived in Bralorne in October. Installation of the crushing circuit is expected to commence in Q1 2027.

For further information, please contact:

Lindsay Dunlop
Vice President, Investor Relations
lindsay.dunlop@taliskerresources.com
+1 647 274 8975

About Talisker Resources Ltd.

Talisker (taliskerresources.com) is a junior resource company involved in the exploration and development of gold projects in British Columbia, Canada. Talisker’s flagship asset is the high-grade, fully permitted Bralorne Gold Project where the Company is producing at the Mustang Mine. Talisker projects also include the Ladner Gold Project, an historic high-grade gold mine near Hope, British Columbia, with significant exploration potential, and the Spences Bridge Project, where the Company has a significant landholding in the emerging Spences Bridge Gold Belt, as well as several other early-stage Greenfields projects.

data.title: Arbonne Appoints David Vanderveen to Chief Executive Officer to Lead Next Phase of Growth
data.description:
Arbonne Appoints David Vanderveen to Chief Executive Officer to Lead Next Phase of Growth

Seasoned entrepreneur brings consumer health and direct selling expertise to lead next chapter.

Arbonne, a global leader in nutrition and wellness, has appointed David Vanderveen as the company’s new Chief Executive Officer effective immediately. Vanderveen is a consumer health and direct selling veteran with more than two decades of experience building global brands and transformational leadership.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118646636/en/

David Vanderveen has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of Arbonne, bringing more than two decades of experience in consumer health and direct selling to lead the company’s next phase of growth and modernization.

Building on more than 46 years of history in beauty and health and wellness, Vanderveen will focus on the company’s modernization efforts, evolving its products, technology and field experience for the future.

“I’m looking forward to creating growth that happens when employees, independent consultants and partners work together,” said Vanderveen. “Our Independent Consultants are the original creators. When corporate and field leadership partner, they can create compelling brands, engaging content and modern tools, which becomes a movement.”

Vanderveen founded XS Energy and built it into a global direct selling brand under Amway. Most recently, he served as President of the Americas at Prenetics, helping scale the supplement brand IM8 to $200 million in 18 months. He has also held executive roles at New Age Beverage Co., Nirvana Water Services and ITWORKS Marketing.

“David was the clear choice as the new executive leadership at Arbonne because he brings both sides of what this role demands: the entrepreneurial instincts of a founder and a deep understanding of network marketing,” said Jean-David Schwartz, Groupe Rocher Chief Executive Officer. “He has built brands and transformed companies. That is exactly the experience we need for Arbonne’s next chapter.”

Vanderveen assumes the role from Jean-David Schwartz, who stepped in as the interim Chief Executive Officer earlier this year.

About Arbonne

Arbonne is a global health and wellness company empowering people to flourish through sustainable, healthy living. Founded in 1980 as a pioneer of the clean beauty movement, Arbonne products are pure, safe, beneficial™. As a Certified B Corporation®, Arbonne maintains a long-standing commitment to sustainability, carefully considering the impact on people, communities, and the planet.

For more information: press@arbonne.com

data.title: U.S. Offers $50 Million to Support Malaysia's Sovereign AI Cloud Initiative
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR--The U.S. plans to help develop Malaysia's sovereign artificial-intelligence cloud, including through the participation of U.S. technology firms.

President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the cooperation on Wednesday.

Trump is in Shenzhen this week as part of his visit to China for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings.

The U.S. indicated its intention to provided $50 million in financing for Malaysia's initiative, as well as technical assistance and training, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said.

The move comes as Malaysia seeks to establish itself as a regional AI hub, attracting billions of dollars in investment from global technology companies amid growing demand for computing power and cloud services.

In budget 2026, the government allocated 2 billion ringgit, or about $486 million, to establish the sovereign AI cloud, underscoring its push to build domestic AI infrastructure and ensure greater control over data and computing resources.

data.title: Toshiba Releases Photovoltaic-Output Photocoupler for Driving High-Voltage Power MOSFETs in Automotive Equipment
data.description:
Toshiba Releases Photovoltaic-Output Photocoupler for Driving High-Voltage Power MOSFETs in Automotive Equipment

– Adjustable turn-off time with an external circuit –

Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage Corporation ("Toshiba") has launched “TLX9909,” a photovoltaic-output photocoupler for solid-state relays (SSRs)[1] in automotive equipment. The new product enables adjustment of turn-off time with an external circuit. Volume shipments start today.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118660977/en/

Toshiba: TLX9909, a photovoltaic-output photocoupler for driving high-voltage power MOSFETs in automotive equipment.

Relay units for automotive equipment are required to offer a longer service life, smaller sizes and higher reliability. The contacts of mechanical relays are subject to wear and contact failure with long-term use, so mechanical relays are increasingly being replaced by SSRs, which have no moving contacts and use semiconductors for switching.

TLX9909 is a photovoltaic-output photocoupler that directly drives the gate of a discrete MOSFET using electric power generated by a photodiode array[2] when it receives light from the input-side LED. As it does not require an isolated-side power supply or a charge-pump circuit, it helps reduce the number of components and contributes to smaller system size and higher reliability.

Although TLX9909 is configured without a built-in control circuit, it maintains an open voltage[3] of 13.5V (min), equivalent to that of the current TLX9910, which does have a built-in control circuit. By selecting an external gate discharge circuit, users can adjust the turn-off time to suit the connected MOSFET and application, bringing greater flexibility to gate control design. In addition, while the current TLX9905 and TLX9906 offer an open voltage of 7V (min), TLX9909 offers a higher open voltage of 13.5V (min). This makes it easier to secure the gate drive voltage for high-voltage power MOSFETs, expanding the range of MOSFETs that it can be combined with.

Combining TLX9909 with an external high-voltage power MOSFET allows flexible configuration of high-voltage, high-current switching circuits, which can be difficult to achieve with photorelays limited by the ratings of their built-in MOSFETs. The availability of both TLX9909, which emphasizes adjustability through external circuits, and TLX9910, which has a built-in discharge circuit, realizes product selection to meet system requirements, such as flexibility in circuit design and the number of components.

The new product complies with AEC-Q101, the reliability standard for automotive electronic components, and is suitable for SSR applications in automotive equipment such as battery management systems (BMS), on-board chargers (OBC), and inverter units.

Toshiba will continue to expand its lineup of photocoupler products that contribute to improving the reliability of automotive and industrial equipment.

Notes:

[1] Solid-state relays (SSRs): The primary (control) side and the secondary (switching) side are electrically isolated by an isolation barrier, which allows switching of circuits directly connected to AC lines, or switching between devices with different ground potentials.

[2] Photodiode array: A light-receiving element consisting of multiple photodiodes connected in series. It receives light from the input LED, generates voltage, and functions as the gate drive power supply for the downstream power semiconductor.

[3] Open voltage: The output voltage obtained when the output terminals of a photovoltaic coupler are open. It serves as an indicator of the gate drive voltage for external MOSFETs.

Applications

  • Automotive equipment
    SSR applications, including battery management systems (BMS), on-board chargers (OBC), inverter units, etc.

Features

  • Adjustable turn-off time using an external gate discharge circuit
  • High open voltage: VOC=13.5V (min)
  • Compliant with AEC-Q101
